# Git
Free and open source distributed version control system designed to handle everything from small to very large projects with speed and efficiency 

![git](data:image/png;base64,)
## Conventional commits
There is a specification for adding human and machine readable meaning to commit messages: https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/. It is possible to use tools like `standard-version` to generate change log based on commit history. This tool parses commit messages and produces structured changelogs. Changelog specification: https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/.
It is also possible to use git trailers in generated changelog when [trailer convention](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-interpret-trailers) is used in commit messages.

Here is the most common conventional commit types:

| Type       | Meaning                                                                 |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `feat`     | A new feature for the user or API                                       |
| `fix`      | A bug fix                                                               |
| `docs`     | Documentation-only changes (README, comments, etc.)                     |
| `style`    | Code style changes (formatting, missing semicolons, etc.) — no logic    |
| `refactor` | Code changes that neither fix a bug nor add a feature                   |
| `perf`     | Performance improvements                                                |
| `test`     | Adding or updating tests                                                |
| `build`    | Changes that affect the build system or external dependencies           |
| `ci`       | Changes to CI configuration files and scripts (GitHub Actions, Travis)  |
| `chore`    | Routine tasks, maintenance, or other changes that don’t modify src/test |
| `revert`   | Reverts a previous commit                                               |
| `config`   | Changes to configuration files (e.g., `.eslintrc`, `.prettierrc`)       |
| `env`      | Environment-specific changes (e.g., Docker, deployment scripts)         |
| `security` | Patches or updates related to vulnerabilities                           |
| `deps`     | Dependency updates                                                      |
| `init`     | Initial commit or project scaffolding                                   |
